cleanIntro: Taurus's 856 book covers four guns in one table - 856, 856UL, 856CH and 856CHUL - and the differences that matter for handling are the action and the weight, not the outside. The 856 and 856UL are DA/SA with an exposed hammer; the CH models are concealed-hammer and double action only. All four are six-shot .38 Special on a 2 or 3 inch barrel, and Taurus publishes NO disassembly for any of them: this is a cylinder-open clean from start to finish.

steps.title: Which 856 is on the bench - hammer or no hammer, steel or UL
steps.action: Read the table before you touch anything. All four models are .38 Special with six chambers on a 2 or 3 inch barrel, but the 856 and 856UL are DA/SA and the 856CH and 856CHUL are double action only. Weight tells you the frame: 22.1 oz for a 2-inch steel gun against 15.7 oz for the UL.
steps.prose: The action distinction is not cosmetic for cleaning. On a DA/SA 856 you can cock the hammer to check timing and to see the transfer bar rise; on a CH there is no hammer spur to cock and you check the same things by riding the trigger through slowly. Knowing which you own before you start stops you concluding a concealed-hammer gun is broken.

steps.title: Thumb piece FORWARD, cylinder out to the left, all six visible
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction and finger off the trigger. Push the thumb piece on the left side of the frame FORWARD with your right thumb, press the cylinder out to the left with your other hand, and look into all six chambers.
steps.prose: Forward is the whole trick and it is where most first-time Taurus owners come unstuck: pressing the thumb piece down or inward simply pins the cylinder shut, and the gun feels seized. It slides toward the muzzle. Once the cylinder is out, keep it out - that swung-out position is the working state for everything that follows, and it is the only access an 856 gives you.
steps.quote:
Revolver Be sure the firearm is completely unloaded and contains no cartridges or cartridge cases. With 
the thumb of the right hand push the thumb piece forward. Then press on the cylinder to swing it to the left. 
Visually check that all six (6) chambers are empty.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Firearms Safety Systems, printed p.9 (PDF p.5)

steps.title: Muzzle UP, one sharp push on the extractor rod
steps.action: With the cylinder fully out, raise the muzzle and press sharply on the extractor rod. All six cases lift together on the star and either drop clear or come out in your fingers. Confirm every one has gone.
steps.prose: Muzzle up, always. With the barrel level or down, a case that only half-lifts slides straight back into its chamber as the star returns, and you finish convinced you have emptied a revolver you have not. One decisive stroke beats three tentative ones - a partial lift is what lets a .38 case tip and re-seat.
steps.quote:
Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure that all fired cartridges are 
ejected. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded (Fig.3).
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Operating Instructions, printed p.21 (PDF p.11)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: Six chambers, and on a CH there is no single action to fall back on
steps.action: Confirm the count: the 856 has six chambers turning around a central axis, and the shots may be fired single action by cocking the hammer or double action by pulling the trigger - except on the CH models, which fire double action only.
steps.prose: This is the line to read carefully if you own an 856CH, because every single-action instruction in the wider Taurus catalog is inapplicable to it. It also changes the function check at the end: on a CH the only way to verify the cylinder indexes and locks is a slow, full double-action stroke with an empty, swung-in cylinder.
steps.aside: The 856CH models can only be fired in double action.
steps.quote:
The Taurus 856 revolvers have a swing out type cylinder with six (6) chambers, turning around a central 
axis which allows you to fire six shots.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Operating Instructions, printed p.21 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: Look AND feel every chamber - that is the working state
steps.action: Before any solvent comes out: muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, thumb piece depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and the revolver confirmed unloaded by looking into AND feeling each chamber.
steps.prose: A fingertip finds what bench light hides. A brass case head sitting deep in a .38 chamber reads as chamber wall to the eye at the wrong angle, and an 856's chambers are short enough that a case sits almost flush. From here the cylinder stays out; nothing else on this revolver opens.
steps.quote:
Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, 
(3) depress the thumb piece and completely swing out the cylinder, (4) ensure the firearm is completely 
unloaded by looking and feeling each chamber.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: The Model 856 is one of the few Taurus revolvers rated for +P
steps.action: If you shoot +P .38 Special through this gun, confirm it is actually on Taurus's list - the Model 856 in 38 Special is named there by model. Taurus is equally clear that firing +P in a Taurus product that is NOT on that list may be dangerous.
steps.prose: Being on the list is permission, not advice: the same page says +P generates pressures well above standard and that unless you need it you should not use it, particularly for practice. For cleaning it has a practical consequence - a diet of +P puts more carbon on the cylinder face and more flame cutting at the topstrap, so check both every time.
steps.quote:
Firing +P ammunition in other Taurus products may be dangerous and can result in serious 
bodily injury or death.
Model 85 small-frame revolver in 38 Special. 
Model 856 revolvers in 38 Special.

steps.title: An 856 is not every small revolver that looks like one
steps.action: Do not carry this procedure onto another snub-nosed .38 because it is the same shape. Taurus's own warning is that look-alike firearms differ in the location and function of their controls, and the forward-sliding thumb piece is the obvious example - most other makes' cylinder latches push rearward or inward.
steps.prose: The tell is always a control that behaves the other way. If pushing the latch toward the muzzle does nothing, stop rather than pushing harder: you are holding a different gun and the correct motion for it is somewhere else on the frame.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Ammunition, printed p.19 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: Every 200 rounds, and check the screws while you are in there
steps.action: Clean and lubricate at least every 200 rounds, and check for loose screws or pins at the same time - tighten screws and press pins back in as needed. On an 856 the screws worth your attention are the sideplate screw, the yoke screw and the grip screw.
steps.prose: Two hundred rounds is a light range session with a six-shooter, and a lightweight 856UL reaches the interval faster in felt terms because it beats itself harder for the same load. The grip screw in particular walks on the alloy-framed guns; a loose grip on a snub is felt as a shifting point of impact before it is noticed as a maintenance item.
steps.quote:
The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without any disassembly steps. For 
Optimal performance, we recommend you clean and lubricate your firearm for at least every 200 rounds 
fired through the firearm for optimal performance. At the same time check for any lose screws or pins. 
Tighten the screws and press pins back in as needed.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Field strip complete - the 856 does not come apart
steps.action: Cylinder swung out, six chambers confirmed empty, and that is the entire strip. Taurus publishes no disassembly for the 856 at all and states the revolver is cleaned and lubricated without any disassembly steps, so the sideplate stays on and the yoke stays in.
steps.prose: The part list in the back runs from the cylinder assembly through the transfer bar to the sideplate screw, and none of it comes with an order of operations - it is a list for ordering, not an invitation. If an 856 needs to be opened, the book's route is a qualified gunsmith or Taurus Customer Care, and unauthorised parts replacement voids the warranty.
steps.quote: The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without any disassembly steps.

deepAbsentReason: The Taurus 856 book publishes no disassembly at all. It states that the firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions WITHOUT any disassembly steps, asks for a clean every 200 rounds with a check for loose screws and pins, and gives a four-item routine: brass brush and solvent through bore and chambers, a dry patch, a non-abrasive exterior wipe, and a lightly oiled cloth. The exploded view and part list at the back are for ordering parts and carry no sequence; the book routes malfunctions and repairs to a qualified gunsmith or to Taurus Customer Care. There is therefore nothing deeper to walk, and inventing a sideplate procedure would be inventing the manufacturer's words.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chambers with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent, then run a dry cotton patch through
Do all six chambers, not just the bore - a .38 chamber that has carried lead loads builds a ring at the case mouth that makes extraction sticky
On a 2-inch 856 a single stroke covers the whole bore, so slow down rather than speeding up; the forcing cone just ahead of the gap needs the brush turned into it
Hold the barrel to a light and confirm a clear bore before the revolver is put away

cleaning.name: CYLINDER FACE, STAR & FRAME WINDOW
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cloth and clear residue from small crevices with a small brush
Work the carbon ring off the FRONT face of the cylinder - on a .38 snub it is the deposit that eventually stops the cylinder closing
Push the extractor rod back and clean behind the star; grit under the star is what makes a cylinder refuse to index
Wipe the barrel/cylinder gap area, the forcing cone and the topstrap above it, and look for flame cutting on a gun fed +P

cleaning.name: OIL, SCREWS & STORAGE
tasks: After cleaning, rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth for a thin protective film
A drop of oil at the crane and on the moving parts - a drop, not a flood, which only migrates into the lockwork
Check the sideplate, yoke and grip screws are tight and press any proud pins back in
A revolver fitted with a laser must not be cleaned in a well or ultrasonic machine that submerges it

reassembly: Nothing came off, so nothing goes back on. Let the extractor rod re-seat fully before the cylinder goes home.
Close the cylinder gently but firmly until it latches - never flick it open or snap it shut, which knocks the crane out of true and starts a cylinder dragging.
Rotate the closed cylinder by hand and feel it index and lock into each of the six notches before the revolver is stored.
fncheck: With all six chambers confirmed empty: the cylinder should latch with light thumb pressure and show no perceptible side play; hand-rotating it should feel the cylinder stop drop into each notch; on a DA/SA 856 the hammer should hold at full cock and the transfer bar should rise only as the trigger goes fully through, and on an 856CH the same is checked by riding the double-action stroke slowly. Both actions must reset positively when the trigger returns all the way forward. Taurus's standing advice is that a Taurus revolver is carried with an empty chamber under the hammer, and never with the hammer cocked or the trigger held to the rear.
